messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 54 omitted, sha256 146656ab16fda879>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 92
reason: The document defines confidential information broadly, including non-technical items such as administrative and commercial facts, customer details, and records, and says the definition is not limited to the listed items, so it is not restricted to technical information.
<quote check="exact">The term 'confidential information' includes, but is not limited to, all documents, drawings, data, subjects, information, records, knowhow, protected rights, inventions, ideas, concepts, knowledge, technology, design, specifications</quote>
<quote check="exact">all documents and information concerning the company, in particular administrative and commercial facts and details concerning customers, products, suppliers and other business partners</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 96
reason: The definition of confidential information expressly includes administrative and commercial information and is 'not limited to' technical items, so it is not restricted to technical information.
<quote check="exact">all documents and information concerning the company, in particular administrative and commercial facts and details concerning customers, products, suppliers and other business partners</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 95
reason: The definition of confidential information expressly covers non-technical business information such as administrative and commercial facts, so it is not limited to technical information.
<quote check="exact">all documents and information concerning the company, in particular administrative and commercial facts and details concerning customers, products, suppliers and other business partners</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label":"Contradiction","confidence":95,"quotes":["all documents and information concerning the company, in particular administrative and commercial facts and details concerning customers, products, suppliers and other business partners"],"reason":"The definition of confidential information expressly covers non-technical administrative and commercial business information, so it is not limited to technical information."}
